title: Heinfels Castle East Tyrol
name: Heinfels Castle East Tyrol
kurzbeschreibung: Burg Heinfels in East Tyrol's Hochpustertal: the 'Queen of the Pustertal' perched on a steep rocky hill with a modern museum and panoramic circular tour.
beschreibung:
Overview

The majestic Burg Heinfels perches high on a striking rocky outcrop at 1,130 metres above sea level over the municipality of Heinfels at the gateway to the Villgratental in the East Tyrolean Hochpustertal (Bezirk Lienz). Due to its commanding, impregnable position visible from afar, this formidable fortress has for centuries been reverently hailed as the “Queen of the Pustertal”. Following years of meticulous, heritage-compliant restoration, the historic castle grounds reopened in the summer of 2020 in renewed splendour and rank among the premier cultural excursion destinations in East Tyrol.

History, Architecture & Museum

According to legend, the stronghold was founded as early as the 5th century by the Huns; its first documentary record dates to 1243 as a possession of the Bishops of Brixen and the Counts of Görz. For centuries, Heinfels served as a military bulwark controlling the Pustertal road into Italy. The complex comprises a High Medieval inner ward with a formidable keep, a Late Gothic residential palace and extensive Renaissance outer walls with gun towers. Inside, a state-of-the-art museum tour equipped with interactive multimedia stations guides visitors through centuries of turbulent history: wander through historical knight and court chambers, discover the Gothic castle chapel of St. Laurentius, and climb the keep for panoramic vistas across the Karnische Alpen and the Lienzer Dolomiten.

Visit & Getting There

Burg Heinfels is open during the summer season from early May to late October, Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 17:00 (closed Mondays; open daily in July and August). Self-guided exploration with audio guide or participating in guided tours. Admission fees (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €10.00, seniors approx. €8.50, children (aged 6 to 14) approx. €5.00, family ticket approx. €24.00. Holders of the regional Glockner-Dolomiten Card receive discounted entry. Getting there by car: via the B100 (Drautalstraße) from Lienz or from South Tyrol/Innichen directly to Heinfels; parking is available at the base of the castle hill in the valley. On foot, a gentle panoramic path leads up to the castle gate in about 10 minutes. By public transport: ÖBB/S-Bahn to Sillian station, followed by an easy 15-minute walk.

Tips

Parts of the outer grounds and the castle restaurant offer low-barrier access; the historic ascent up the keep requires navigating stairs. Combine your visit with a detour to the famous covered Punbrücke – East Tyrol's longest historic timber bridge – situated directly at the foot of the castle hill.
